tourSteps.0: GITEX Global 2025, day 1 at Dubai World Trade Centre. Watch the corridor through the day in the 3D twin.
tourSteps.1: What if it is a hot day? More visitors take the metro, and World Trade Centre station rises above its threshold ring.
tourSteps.2: AI agents propose plans, and the simulator measures each one.
tourSteps.3: You stay in charge: approving the top plan brings every station back under the ring.
tourSteps.4: Try rain, a custom event, or build your own plan in the My plan tab.

glfail: 3D needs WebGL, which is not available in this browser. The table view shows the same results.
canvasAria: 3D digital twin of the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor. Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom, tap a station to select it. The table view shows the same data.
apiDown: The planning service is not reachable. Showing the last saved results; reconnecting automatically.
publicDemo: Public research demo by SP Jain students. Baseline demand is synthetic and scenario values are assumptions. Not an RTA system and not endorsed by RTA.
how1: Forecast: background demand per station and hour, plus an event surge shared across stations by walking distance.
how2: Capacity: trains per hour from the RTA timetable × train capacity × the share available at one station. Station-hours above the comfort threshold are flagged.
how3: Specialist AI agents choose from a menu of measures (extra trains, wayfinding, feeder shuttles, robotaxi staging, staggered exits, entry metering) and size each one from the forecast crowd; a critic sends back what falls short.
how4: A deterministic simulator scores every plan. The agents never calculate numbers; every figure is checked.
how5: Nothing is applied until a human approves it, and every decision is logged.
howAlign: Designed around RTA AI Strategy priorities: congestion reduction, agentic AI and human approval of every decision.
creditsNote: {n} buildings in the 20 km ring; {e} of them have no height in any dataset and use an ESTIMATED height.
footer: Research prototype by SP Jain MAIB students. Baseline demand is synthetic; attendance, metro share and capacity values are assumptions. Train frequency: RTA open data (GTFS). Map: © OpenStreetMap contributors; building heights are estimated where untagged; landmark models are approximations. Not an RTA system and not endorsed by RTA.

chat.best: The team recommends option {rank_n}, “{title_s}”: riders over the line {excess_b_n} → {excess_a_n}, peak load {peak_b_pct}% → {peak_a_pct}%.
chat.bestChecks: It passed {passed_n} of {applicable_n} checks and holds in {holds_n} of {total_n} stress cases. Nothing is applied until you approve it in the AI plan tab.
chat.compare: The {shown_n} options the team offered, out of {tested_n} plans it simulated.
chat.notMeasured: The twin does not measure {what_s}, so it cannot rank plans by it. Saying otherwise would be a guess.
chat.lensTop: For {lens_s}: “{title_s}”. Peak load {peak_pct}%, {excess_n} riders over the line, longest wait {wait_x} min, cost index {cost_x}, {parties_n} team(s) must act.
chat.lensClosest: The nearest measured stand-ins are cost and resources. On those: “{title_s}” (cost index {cost_x}, {parties_n} team(s) must act).
chat.lensSame: That is also the team's recommendation.
chat.lensDiffers: The team's overall recommendation is different: “{rec_s}”. It weighs relief against cost.
chat.lensNotOffered: The team simulated this plan but did not offer it: it was outranked on relief against cost. Its recommendation is “{rec_s}”.
chat.lensBlocked: {blocked_n} plan(s) are left out because they break a hard limit. No weighting can bring them back.
chat.noEvent: This scenario has no event, so there is no crowd size to change.
chat.outOfRange: {field_s} must be between {min_n} and {max_n}. You asked for {value_n}.
chat.outOfRangePct: {field_s} must be between {min_pct}% and {max_pct}%. You asked for {value_pct}%.
chat.whatifAtt: With {att_a_n} visitors instead of {att_b_n}: station-hours over the line {over_b_x} → {over_a_x}, peak load {peak_b_pct}% → {peak_a_pct}% (worst at {worst_st}).
chat.notApplied: This is a what-if. The scenario on screen has not changed.
chat.needThreshold: Which comfort line? The slider goes from {min_pct}% to {max_pct}%.
chat.whatifThr: With a {thr_a_pct}% comfort line instead of {thr_b_pct}%: station-hours over the line {over_b_x} → {over_a_x}, stations over it {st_b_n} → {st_a_n}. The crowd is the same; only the line moves.
chat.break: The corridor crosses the line at about {att_n} visitors, first at {station_st}. This scenario has {now_n}.
chat.noBreak: No station crosses the line at any crowd size in this scenario.
chat.if_hot: On a hot day: station-hours over the line {over_b_x} → {over_a_x}, peak load {peak_b_pct}% → {peak_a_pct}%.
chat.if_rain: If it rains: station-hours over the line {over_b_x} → {over_a_x}, peak load {peak_b_pct}% → {peak_a_pct}%.
chat.road: Road pressure peaks at {veh_n} extra cars an hour at {hour_t}, {pressure_pct}% of one direction of Sheikh Zayed Road. This is a proxy, not a traffic model.
chat.confidenceSynthetic: Demand is synthetic, so this cannot be higher than low, however well the plan tests. It shows the method works, not that the figures are right.
chat.evidenceData: The forecast uses synthetic demand ({dataset_s}). It is labelled synthetic everywhere.
chat.evidenceBand: At {station_st} at {hour_t} the forecast expects {p50_n} riders, between {p10_n} and {p90_n} on most days.
chat.evidenceBacktest: In its last backtest the offline forecaster scored {mase_x} against {naive_x} for a simple seasonal guess (lower is better), with {coverage_pct}% of {rows_n} held-out hours inside its range. That test was on synthetic data too.
chat.evidenceBacktestServed: In its last backtest the forecast shown on screen scored {mase_x} against {naive_x} for a simple seasonal guess (lower is better), with {coverage_pct}% of {rows_n} held-out hours inside its range. That test was on synthetic data too.
chat.evidenceNarrow: That range is meant to hold four hours in five and held only {coverage_pct}%, so it is too narrow. Treat the forecast's spread as low confidence.
chat.noChange: I have no earlier scenario in this conversation to compare with. Change a setting, then ask again.
chat.changedEffect: Before any plan, that moved the peak load {peak_b_pct}% → {peak_a_pct}% and the station-hours over the line {over_b_x} → {over_a_x} (worst at {worst_st}).
chat.changedPlan: So the recommendation changed from “{rec_b_s}” to “{rec_a_s}”: the first no longer gives the best relief for its cost.
chat.changedPlanNow: Before, no plan was needed. Now the team recommends “{rec_s}”.
chat.changedPlanGone: Before, the team recommended “{rec_s}”. Now no station crosses the line, so no plan is needed.
chat.editNothing: I could not find a setting to change in that. You can set attendance, the exit window, the comfort line, the weather, the share by metro or the priority.
chat.confirmThreshold: A {to_pct}% comfort line is above {limit_pct}%. Raising the line hides crowding instead of reducing it. Apply it anyway?
chat.editRejected: The forecast did not accept those values, so nothing was changed. ({why_s})
chat.applied: Done. {changes_n} setting(s) changed; this is scenario v{version_n}.
chat.undone: Undone. {changes_n} setting(s) put back; this is scenario v{version_n}.

readAs.safety: There is no “safety” setting: I read it as “most relief”. Ask “Which plan is safest?” to compare plans on safety.

chat.effect: With no plan in place: peak load {peak_b_pct}% → {peak_a_pct}%, station-hours over the line {over_b_x} → {over_a_x} (worst at {worst_st}).
chat.plansCleared: Earlier plans were for the old scenario and have been cleared. Ask the team for a new one.
chat.nothingToUndo: There is no change of mine to undo.
chat.noDocument: I have no document that answers that.
chat.fromDocuments: From {docs_n} document(s). These explain the method or quote what the authority publishes. No figure in the twin is taken from them.
chat.help: Ask about crowding, plans, what-ifs, confidence or evidence for this scenario. Or tell me a change, such as “attendance to sixty thousand”.
chat.refuse: I only answer questions about crowding on this corridor and this twin.
chat.refuseInjection: Part of that read like an instruction to the system, so I changed nothing. Say the change again in plain words.

kiosk.noAnswer: I do not have a reliable answer to that. Please ask the team at the stand, or check official RTA channels.
kiosk.staffOnly: That is for the planning team, not the visitor screen. Tap a question below.
kiosk.accessNote: For step-free access: the twin does not know the state of each lift. Ask station staff on the day.
kiosk.useAlt: At {hour_t}, {station_st} is at {load_pct}%. {alt_st} is quieter, at {alt_pct}%, about {walk_n} minutes' walk away.

use.easy: {station_st} is easy at {hour_t}: load {load_pct}%, no real wait.
use.busy: {station_st} is busy at {hour_t} (load {load_pct}%) but still your best choice nearby.
use.crowded: {station_st} is crowded at {hour_t} (load {load_pct}%). No quieter station is within walking distance; leaving later helps most.

kiosk.leaveNow: You can leave at {hour_t}: {station_st} is at {load_pct}%.
kiosk.leaveLater: {station_st} is at {load_pct}% at {hour_t}. From {later_t} it is easy again.
kiosk.leaveBusy: {station_st} is at {load_pct}% at {hour_t} and stays busy for the next hours. A nearby station may be quieter.
kiosk.noOptions: No other station is within walking distance of {station_st}.
kiosk.optionsNote: The twin covers the metro only. For buses and taxis, check official RTA channels.
kiosk.access: Here is what RTA publishes about access on the metro.
kiosk.accessQuieter: For more room at {hour_t}: {alt_st} is quieter than {station_st}, about {walk_n} minutes' walk away.
kiosk.reachAsk: Which station are you going to?
kiosk.reachUnknown: I only know the six stations of this corridor. Which of them is nearest to where you are going?
kiosk.reachChange: From {from_st} to {to_st}: {stops_n} stops with {changes_n} change(s), starting on the {line_s}.
kiosk.reachNote: Stops are counted from the metro map. For directions and times, check official RTA channels.
kiosk.busiest: The busiest moment is {station_st} at {hour_t}, at {peak_pct}%.
kiosk.title: Ask about your trip
kiosk.source: From the simulator and RTA's public pages. Synthetic demand: not live travel advice.
